subject: radiology
title: Biliary and urinary drainage

steps.tx: Obstructed bile needs a route out when endoscopy cannot drain the system. **Percutaneous transhepatic biliary drainage** punctures a peripheral duct under ultrasound and fluoroscopy after failed endoscopic drainage or in hilar obstruction. An **internal external catheter** drains into a bag while its side holes stent past the block into the duodenum. Left sided access suits hilar tumours, while right sided access suits distal blocks, and **cholangitis** with fever, pain and jaundice makes drainage urgent.
steps.say: Obstructed bile needs a route out when endoscopy cannot drain the system. Biliary drainage punctures a peripheral duct under imaging after failed endoscopic drainage. The catheter drains into a bag while side holes stent past the block. Fever with pain and jaundice makes drainage urgent and changes elective plans into emergency care.

steps.tx: An infected obstructed kidney is a true emergency that needs urgent drainage. **Percutaneous nephrostomy** drains pus under ultrasound within hours in **obstructive pyelonephritis** and saves kidney and life. **Antegrade ureteric stenting** follows once sepsis settles and pushes a double J stent down to the bladder. Pregnancy with obstructing stones favours nephrostomy over radiation heavy options. A clotted or displaced tube gives falling output with pain and fever and needs exchange.
steps.say: An infected obstructed kidney is a true emergency that needs urgent drainage. Nephrostomy drains pus under ultrasound within hours and saves kidney function. Antegrade stenting follows once sepsis settles and restores internal drainage. Pregnancy with obstructing stones favours nephrostomy, while a blocked tube needs exchange rather than antibiotics alone.

steps.tx: The main ultrasound shows an **obstructed infected kidney** with a curled **percutaneous nephrostomy** pigtail sitting inside the dilated collecting system. Echogenic material labelled as pus under pressure explains why drainage cannot wait for stone surgery. The small inset shows later **antegrade stenting** with a double J stent passing down the ureter. The sequence teaches emergency drainage first and definitive internal drainage after sepsis settles.
steps.say: The ultrasound shows an infected obstructed kidney with a nephrostomy pigtail inside it. Material under pressure explains why drainage cannot wait for stone surgery. The inset shows later antegrade stenting with a stent down the ureter. The sequence is logical because emergency drainage comes first and internal drainage follows later.

vis.alt: Ultrasound of infected obstructed kidney with nephrostomy pigtail and inset fluoroscopy of antegrade ureteric stent.
vis.caption: Ultrasound and fluoroscopy of nephrostomy and antegrade stenting. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Gallbladder and abscess drains buy time safely in patients unfit for surgery. **Percutaneous cholecystostomy** decompresses acute cholecystitis, with interval gallbladder surgery planned later for suitable patients. **Abscess drainage** uses a **pigtail catheter** that is upsized or flushed when thick pus slows output. Pancreatic collections need a planned route that respects vessels and bowel on cross sectional imaging. Flushing, secure fixation and output charts prevent blockage and accidental removal.
steps.say: Gallbladder and abscess drains buy time safely in patients unfit for surgery. Cholecystostomy decompresses the inflamed gallbladder and allows later planned surgery. Abscess drainage uses a pigtail catheter that needs flushing when pus thickens. Careful route planning protects vessels and bowel, while fixation and charts prevent blockage and accidental removal.

vis.alt: Diagram showing percutaneous cholecystostomy catheter in gallbladder and pigtail catheter draining an abscess.
vis.caption: Percutaneous cholecystostomy and abscess drainage techniques. Image: Zhang, H., Wen, Xd., Ma, X. et al., CC BY 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.tx: Metal stents keep malignant biliary strictures open for longer than plastic stents. **Self expanding metal stents** give longer patency and fewer exchanges in **malignant obstruction**. Benign strictures from stones or surgery may remodel with prolonged plastic stents or retrievable covered metal stents. **Stent occlusion** returns with jaundice, itch and cholangitis and needs exchange through the mature tract. Bleeding into bile after puncture usually settles, but an arterial pseudoaneurysm needs coil embolisation.
steps.say: Metal stents keep malignant biliary strictures open for longer than plastic stents. Metal gives longer patency and needs fewer exchanges in malignant obstruction. Benign strictures may remodel with prolonged or retrievable stents over time. Occlusion returns with jaundice and itch and needs exchange, while arterial bleeding needs coil embolisation promptly.
